key_method: osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to key code N'
notes: Key code 144 = brightness up, 145 = brightness down on the built-in display; one press = 1/16 (0.0625) of the DisplayServices scale; the OSD HUD appears.

Read method that tracks key presses: DisplayServicesGetBrightness (private DisplayServices.framework, ctypes). CoreDisplay_Display_GetUserBrightness stayed at 1.0 during the presses, so it is NOT a valid read-back.
Restore: DisplayServicesSetBrightness(display, before) works without key presses (after_restore == before).
At 1.0, key 144 is a no-op (already max); verify 'brighter' as value > before OR before == 1.0.

External display as main: NOT TESTED - only the built-in 'Color LCD' was connected (Samsung 'The Frame' is a Bluetooth/AirPlay device, not attached). Per plan 7.3 external displays stay operator-only.
Keys go through System Events, so the daemon needs Accessibility (iTerm has it). No Safari or app focus needed.
plan_verdict: pass: key codes 144/145 change the built-in display -> set_brightness(step) stays on the fast path; external display -> operator.
